extracted.intended_audience: health journalists, consumers interested in critically evaluating health news and press releases, and potential supporters/donors
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational overview describing the mission, scope, policies and high-level evaluative aims of HealthNewsReview.org for assessing health care journalism, PR, advertising and related messages. It orients journalists and consumers to the site's criteria, star-score system, and operational limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, balanced and complete information about tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org promotes the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and evaluations should emphasize whether reporting or messaging provides complete and balanced evidence and clearly communicates benefits, harms, uncertainties and tradeoffs to support shared decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The site aims to help consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions and to provide criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should enable lay readers to judge the strength of claims, understand study limitations, and identify potential exaggeration or misrepresentation in news, PR, advertising and marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote shared decision‑making principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A core goal is promoting the principles of shared decision-making so individuals receive information that allows choices informed by tradeoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should assess whether communications facilitate informed choices rather than simply promoting a single option or oversimplifying complex decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: evaluate journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other consumer-directed messages
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review framework is applied across multiple message types (news stories, news releases, ads, PR), with attention to how each may influence consumer perceptions and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational role limits: not a definitive medical forum or provider of medical advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science and does not give medical advice or act as an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews focus on accuracy and quality of messaging rather than providing clinical recommendations; reviewers avoid promoting treatments or advocacy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advertising and no product promotion in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org does not accept advertising and will not allow commenters to promote products on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve editorial independence and avoid conflicts, commercial promotion is excluded from site content and community interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence from funders
rubrics_metrics.description: No funder has ever had, nor will they ever have, any editorial control over the operation of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding sources are disclosed, but evaluations and editorial decisions are kept independent; reviewers and content maintain separation from sponsor influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical selection constraint due to limited staff and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The project cannot review every story or every promotional message because of limited staff (two full-time editorial staff historically) and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should expect selective coverage; the site prioritizes reviews and retains discretion about what to evaluate given capacity limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explicit review criteria and a star-score system (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site refers to specific 'review criteria' and explains 'how the star score is determined' as part of its evaluative approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While detailed criteria and scoring are provided on linked pages (not included here), the organization signals it applies a structured checklist and star-rating to assess quality of health news and releases.
